issue: Two official Rent Board pages give different banking waiting periods
detail: The “Banked rent increases” page says a skipped increase is banked only if “at least 24 full months pass without any rent increase” [[S11]]; Rule 4.12 and the “Learn about rent increases” page say a full 12 months must elapse [[S9]] [[S1]].
what_it_affects: Unit A's 2026-02-01 allowance and any future skipped year.
recommended_action: Ask the Rent Board counsellor which is current, and whether the 1/13/26 rule amendments changed Rule 4.12. Until then, treat the earlier year as at risk if the anniversary date is moved.

issue: Board of Supervisors File No. 261020 - proposed 10% cap, not enacted
detail: The official legislative record was opened on 10 November 2026. It shows a proposal introduced on 15 September 2026, status Pending Committee Action, and no final action. The Rent Board's 9 November notice says the proposal would temporarily cap combined banked and capital-improvement increases at 10% per year; no enactment date or final text is asserted. [[S33]] [[S1]]
what_it_affects: Would change the conditional 13.1% Unit B illustration if enacted as proposed; no amount is cleared for service.
recommended_action: Recheck the official legislative record and the Rent Board notice immediately before any banked increase; see consolidated-hub flag F09. This archived flag is superseded by that current disclosure.

issue: Unit A base rent of $3,995.00 set on 2025-02-01 — lawfulness unverified
detail: A new-tenancy initial rent may be set without limit for an empty unit [[S1]], but the ordinance withdraws that for five years where the prior tenancy ended by an owner notice under Civil Code §1946.1 or a §827 change of terms [[S5]]. How the prior tenancy ended was not supplied.
what_it_affects: If the reset was unavailable, every figure computed from $3,995.00 is wrong.
recommended_action: Obtain the document that ended the prior tenancy (notice, surrender, buyout or vacate letter) and the prior rent history; if it was an owner no-fault notice, recompute from the prior lawful rent.

issue: Tenant A2 is a continuing occupant, not an original lessee
detail: Whether a Rules & Regs §6.14 notice or a Costa-Hawkins reset was ever served on Tenant A2 is unknown. That determines whether a new tenancy was created for rent purposes when the last original occupant left [[S24]].
what_it_affects: Changes both the base rent and the anniversary date for Unit A.
recommended_action: Search the file for a §6.14 notice. If none was served within a reasonable time of learning of the occupancy, obtain advice before treating the base rent as settled.

issue: HUD Fair Market Rent for this ZIP area — no official value confirmed
detail: The FY2026/27 HUD FMR summary page rendered without values and the API requires a token. Secondary sites give $2,850, $3,174, $3,604 and $3,697 for a two-bedroom unit.
what_it_affects: Market context only; it does not change the lawful maximum.
recommended_action: Look the figure up directly on huduser.gov, or treat market comparison as out of scope. The value is intentionally blank on this site.

issue: Rent Board fee payment is not tied to increase validity in Chapter 37
detail: §37.15(e) ties the licence to Housing Inventory reporting [[S4]]. No provision was found in Chapter 37 making an increase void for non-payment of the Chapter 37A fee, although the fee is mandatory and penalties accrue [[S8]].
what_it_affects: Procedural and tenant-relations risk, not an identified legal bar.
recommended_action: Pay the fee by 1 March and keep the receipt. Recorded as an absence-of-authority finding rather than assumed to be a requirement.

issue: No provision requires the same increase across units
detail: Chapter 37 and the Rules were reviewed for an equal-treatment requirement across tenancies [[S18]] [[S5]]. None was found. Discrimination law operates on reason and effect, not on identical percentages [[S25]].
recommended_action: Adopt the written policy on the Owner playbook page and apply it uniformly; have counsel review the decision if only one unit is increased.

issue: Unit A: the 2026-04-01 entry is an assumption, not a fact
detail: The owner's record shows a lease start of 2025-02-01 at $3,995.00, then a “continuing tenancy” dated 2026-04-01 at the same rent for two occupants, one of whom was an original lessee. This site reads that as a partial change of occupants within one continuing tenancy, because a new tenancy for rent purposes requires the last original occupant to vacate or cease permanently residing in the unit [[S24]] [[S5]].
what_it_affects: If it was in fact a wholly new lease with no original occupant remaining, Unit A's anniversary date is 1 April, not 1 February, and the available allowance and effective date change.
recommended_action: Confirm from the signed documents whether Tenant A1 has been in continuous occupancy since 2025-02-01 and whether a new lease was signed in April 2026. If a new tenancy began, recompute: the first increase would be available 2027-04-01.
